summary: Frontend-only verification completed on the public preview URL for the Dispatch Schedule confirmation UX and regressions. The legacy phone/Confirm action is absent; the 5-value confirmation Select opens a pre-filled dialog; saving Declined/Text updates the row and unified Full History; cancelled rows are static; Status, Edit, Cancel, Delete, and New Schedule all worked. One high-impact runtime defect remains: creating/updating a long-reference row triggered a ResizeObserver webpack overlay that blocked normal clicks until the test page overlay was removed for diagnostic continuation.

ui_bugs.component: Dispatch Schedule table / Radix Select flow
ui_bugs.issue: A full-page webpack dev-server runtime overlay appeared after creating a schedule with long client/vendor/post names and using the Confirmation Select. It reported repeated 'ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications' errors and intercepted the Last Modified By click. This is a user-blocking recurrence of the iteration 18 defect.
Create/Edit, Confirmation, and Full History dialogs emit Radix accessibility warnings because DialogContent has no DialogDescription or explicit aria-describedby={undefined}.

action_items: Fix the underlying long-content ResizeObserver/reflow loop and ensure development runtime errors cannot install a click-blocking iframe overlay; re-test create -> confirmation -> Last Modified By using long reference names.
Add DialogDescription or an intentional aria-describedby strategy to Dispatch dialogs.
Add data-testid values to the row Cancel and Del buttons; these required regression controls currently have none.
critical_code_review_comments: The ResizeObserver suppression in frontend/src/index.js uses ordinary bubble-phase window listeners, but the webpack runtime listener is installed earlier and still creates #webpack-dev-server-client-overlay. A capture-phase strategy may prevent the dev overlay, but the underlying unstable table/Select resize loop should also be corrected.

openActions sets actionsDialog before clearing actions, so switching between rows can briefly render the previous schedule's history while the new /actions request is pending; clear actions and show a loading state before opening/fetching.

DispatchSchedulePage retains dead legacy Confirmation History state, API loader, dialog, canHistory permission, and unused Phone/History/ClipboardList imports even though confirmation history is now unified under Full History. Remove the unreachable legacy path.

success_rate.frontend: All requested functional assertions passed; environment not fully green because 1 blocking runtime overlay defect was reproduced

seed_data_creation: Created one isolated TEST_iter21 Dispatch schedule through the UI using existing TEST_ references, changed confirmation to Declined/Text, updated status, edited, cancelled, and permanently deleted it. No test schedule remains.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use admin credentials from /app/memory/test_credentials.md and the public frontend URL. Functional confirmation UX is green. Reproduce the remaining overlay with a newly created row using long TEST_ client/vendor/post names, then choose Declined and click Last Modified By. The overlay occurred in the first end-to-end run and blocked the normal click; a fresh-session diagnostic confirmed the history entry and all regressions, and cleanup succeeded.
rca_of_the_issue: After a long-reference row is inserted and Radix Select/dialog operations cause table reflow, ResizeObserver emits repeated undelivered-notification errors. CRA's webpack-dev-server error client converts them into a full-page iframe overlay that intercepts clicks. The current index.js suppression executes too late/in the ineffective listener phase to reliably stop the already-registered runtime handler. Reproduction: login as super_admin -> create schedule using long TEST_ references -> Confirmation dropdown -> Declined -> save Text/Declined via SMS -> click Last Modified By; normal click timed out because #webpack-dev-server-client-overlay intercepted pointer events.
